verifications.claim: The Environmental Working Group (EWG) released the 2026 "Dirty Dozen".
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Environmental Working Group (EWG) announced their picks... Dirty Dozen lists.'; R4: '2026 "Dirty Dozen"'; R6: 'The Environmental Working Group (EWG)... released its produce report listing the "Dirty Dozen"'; R7: 'Environmental Working Group’s 2026 Shopper’s Guide to Pesticides in Produce.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm EWG released the 2026 Dirty Dozen list.

verifications.claim: According to the 2026 report, spinach has the highest pesticide residues by weight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'spinach holds more pesticide residue by weight than any other type of produce.'; R8: 'Spinach... had more pesticide residue by weight than any other type of produce'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state spinach tops the list for pesticide residue by weight in the 2026 report.

verifications.claim: According to the 2026 report, the items containing the most pesticide residues are spinach, kale, collard and mustard greens, strawberries, grapes, nectarines, peaches, cherries, apples, blackberries, pears, potatoes, and blueberries.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Spinach... kale, collard and mustard greens, strawberries, grapes, nectarines, peaches, cherries, apples, blackberries, pears and blueberries.'; R6: 'Spinach, Kale, collard and mustard greens, Strawberries, Grapes, Nectarines, Peaches, Cherries, Apples, Blackberries, Pears, Potatoes, Blueberries'; R7: 'spinach, kale, collard and mustard greens... strawberries, grapes, and nectarines. Blackberries... Apples, cherries, pears and potatoes'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources list exactly these 12 items as the 2026 Dirty Dozen.

verifications.claim: The 2026 report lists bell peppers and hot peppers as additional high-residue items.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'We included green beans and peppers because of their place just below the list'; R3: 'bell peppers; hot peppers'; R6: 'Additional... bell and hot peppers.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm bell and hot peppers as additional high-residue items just below the Dirty Dozen.

verifications.claim: The 2026 report lists green beans as an additional high-residue item.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'We included green beans and peppers because of their place just below the list'; R3: 'green beans'; R6: 'Additional... green beans'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm green beans as an additional high-residue item.

verifications.claim: 96% of Dirty Dozen samples contained pesticides.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'nearly all (96%) of these fruits and vegetables samples contained pesticides'; R7: '96% of samples contained pesticides.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state 96% of Dirty Dozen samples contained pesticides.

verifications.claim: For the first time, the 2026 report found that over 60% of samples contained PFAS "forever chemicals".
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'For the first time, the report found more than 60% of the Dirty Dozen samples contained... "forever chemicals"'; R8: 'For the first time, the report found over 60% of all Dirty Dozen samples contain... PFAS'; R2 cited snippet: 'PFAS pesticides were detected on 63% of all Dirty Dozen produce samples.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first time over 60% (e.g., 63%) of Dirty Dozen samples had PFAS.

verifications.claim: PFAS "forever chemicals" take decades to break down.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'the chemicals can take decades, even centuries, to fully break down'; R8: 'take years to decades — even centuries— to completely break down'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe PFAS as taking decades or more to break down.

verifications.claim: The EWG recommends buying organic versions of these items when possible.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'buying organic versions of produce on the Dirty Dozen, when possible.'; R6: 'Buy organic versions of Dirty Dozen produce when possible.'
verifications.reasoning: EWG sources directly recommend organic for Dirty Dozen when possible.

verifications.claim: The top "Clean Fifteen" items for 2026 include avocados, sweet corn, pineapple, onions, papaya, frozen peas, asparagus, honeydew, kiwi, cabbage, mushrooms, mangoes, sweet potatoes, watermelon, carrots.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Pineapple, Sweet corn, Avocados, Papaya, Onions, Sweet peas, Asparagus, Cabbage, Cauliflower, Watermelon, Mangoes, Bananas, Carrots, Mushrooms, Kiwi'; R7: 'Pineapple, sweet corn, and avocados... papaya, onions, frozen sweet peas, asparagus, cabbage, cauliflower, watermelon, mangoes, bananas, carrots, mushrooms, and kiwi'; no mention of honeydew or sweet potatoes, includes cauliflower and bananas instead.
verifications.reasoning: Sources list consistent Clean Fifteen excluding honeydew and sweet potatoes (includes cauliflower, bananas); claim incorrectly attributes these as included items.

verifications.claim: Some experts, like those at The Garden Professors, argue that the EWG list overstates risks by ignoring the low levels of actual exposure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'One of the biggest issues... omit the crucial component of actual risk... Exposure'; 'EWG methodology... lacks scientific credibility'; 'results in unnecessary fear'
verifications.reasoning: The Garden Professors directly argue EWG overstates risks by ignoring exposure levels in risk assessment.
